sections.title: Where it's at
paragraphs: Atti has run my reminders, notes, calendar and morning brief on Telegram since 28 October 2026. Lifebox is an experiment in whether an app's interface can be shaped for each person who uses it. It is planned as Atti's phone app.

expanders.title: What I'm building
paragraphs: An assistant that remembers, keeps my commitments and handles the routine work of my day. Claude is the model; Atti is the harness, the memory, the persona and the channels around it. Tools are tiered by risk, so reads and simple logs just happen. Telegram first; then a console, voice and, later, always-with-you hardware.

expanders.title: What I tried
paragraphs: A small, fast model routed messages until full agent runs took over. Memory search started as a keyword ranker with a fixed test: the right memory came back first for 8 of 9 questions, the bar an embedding model has to beat. A weekly review turns replies I flag into fixes.

expanders.title: What didn't work
paragraphs: The outbox gave up after about seven minutes and silently lost nudges; it now retries until a deadline. Forwarded messages triggered actions; now they are saved as notes. Message text leaked into commit subjects; subjects are now fixed words.

expanders.title: Open questions and next
paragraphs: A console for heavier work like planning. Hands-free voice sessions; the spec is written. Lifebox as the phone app, where the open problem is one iOS build per person, at 30 to 60 minutes each. Later, hardware. Whether it ever goes beyond me is open.
